title: Dynamic memory cadence for shared GPU safety
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Context: Serving runtime must allocate GPU memory across model weights, KV cache, and activations while supporting continuous batching. Current static headroom allocations cause either wasted reserved memory or frequent OOMs during bursty traffic. Goal: implement a time-cadenced headroom recalculation and transactional per-tenant soft budgets that reconcile with the KV eviction/aging policy to improve utilization and reduce OOM rate.

Scope: algorithm and runtime changes in the scheduler and memory allocator; telemetry and SLOs; migration plan for rolling changes across running hosts. Not in scope: model weight compression (separate project).
implementation_plan:
1) Introduce a "headroom cadence" process that periodically (every 500ms by default) recomputes soft budgets per GPU for weights/KV/activations based on recent allocation trends, tail latency SLO, and tenant priority.
2) Maintain per-tenant transactional soft-reservations: an atomic budget token is acquired when a request is admitted and released when the activation completes; transient overdrafts allowed up to a configurable burst factor with proportional eviction signals.
3) KV cache reclamation policy integration: eviction tiers based on age and per-tenant priority; when cadence signals low headroom, aggressively demote low-priority KV entries and pre-serialize small hot prefixes to host memory.
4) Continuous batching adaptation: batch sizes are adjusted respecting the active headroom; the batcher will split long sequences to avoid large activations under constrained headroom.
5) Telemetry: per-cadence snapshot metrics (allocations, free headroom, evictions, overdrafts) and a cardinality-filtered stream for heavy tenants.
6) Safe rollout: feature gate + telemetry feature flag, start with non-production pool and ramp to 25/50/100% hosts with automated rollback on OOM spike.
design_decisions:
- Cadence interval chosen at 500ms after perf experiments: shorter intervals add jitter and CPU overhead; longer intervals miss fast bursts.
- Allowing controlled overdraft (burst factor 1.2) reduces rejected requests while keeping OOM tail bounded.
- Prefer demotion of KV entries over weight offload because weight offload increases IO and tail latency.
- Use host-memory staging for small hot KV prefixes as a low-latency fallback when GPU headroom is depleted.
tradeoffs:
- Increased CPU work for cadence calculation and bookkeeping versus higher GPU utilization.
- Slightly more complex correctness model due to transactional soft budgets; requires careful instrumentation and testing.
- Pre-serialization to host memory increases PCIe bandwidth usage in peak patterns.
acceptance_criteria:
- OOMs attributable to headroom imbalance reduced by >= 60% on canary pool compared to baseline for mixed workloads.
- 95th percentile tail latency degradation <= 5% for high-priority tenants under burst tests.
- Telemetry shows stable headroom utilization with reduced idle reserved memory across fleets.
- Rollout can be automated with a single feature flag and rollback threshold defined.
metrics:
- OOM_rate_headroom (per-host per-hour)
- headroom_utilization_percentile (50/90/95)
- eviction_rate_kv_per_sec
- overdraft_count_and_duration
- batch_split_frequency
- tail_latency_p95_per_tenant
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: disabled behind feature flag, unit tests and integration tests (local).
Phase 1: start canary on non-prod cluster (10 hosts) for 2 days with strict alarms.
Phase 2: enable on 25% hosts for 3 days, monitor metrics and SLOs.
Phase 3: 50% ramp, run stress suite including synthetic burst & multi-tenant mix.
Phase 4: full rollout with automated OOM rollback (if OOM_rate_headroom > baseline * 1.4 for 5m).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for transactional budget acquire/release and overdraft accounting.
- Integration tests: simulated multi-tenant requests with continuous batching to validate eviction and batch splitting.
- Chaos tests: induce sudden multi-tenant burst, network slowdowns for host-memory path.
- Performance benchmark: measure CPU overhead of cadence at 1000 hosts scale using scaled simulation.
observability:
- Expose per-cadence snapshot metric stream and logs.
- Add tracing spans for budget lifecycle (acquire, overdraft, release, eviction triggered).
- Console dashboards: headroom heatmap, tenant overdraft leaderboard, KV eviction waterfall.
- Alerts: OOM_rate_headroom, sudden increase in overdraft_duration, PCIe utilization above 85%.
